scenario.name: Remote benign SCT execution through regsvr32 and scrobj.dll
scenario.description: The signed regsvr32 utility retrieved a benign lab-only SCT whose JScript launched cmd.exe to write a marker file.

sensors.name: Sysmon
sensors.config_notes: Verification-grade unfiltered process, network, DNS, file, and registry coverage; LSASS ProcessAccess EID 10 enabled.

tool.name: regsvr32.exe
tool.source: Built into the target operating system

staged_file.name: benign.sct
staged_file.content: Benign XML scriptlet whose JScript launches cmd.exe only to write a marker

commands.exit_assessment: The remote SCT executed and wrote its marker before regsvr32 returned 5 after taking the /u unregister path; the exact cause of that final code was not separately diagnosed.

observed_techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Regsvr32
observed_techniques.observation: The signed regsvr32 binary fetched an SCT through scrobj.dll, initialized JScript, and spawned cmd.exe from the scriptlet.

network.assessment: Sysmon linked the TCP connection to regsvr32. Zeek and Suricata decoded a successful SCT GET with the legacy MSIE 7.0/Trident 7.0 User-Agent. DNS was absent because the URL used an IP literal.

files.assessment: Regsvr32 wrote the SCT to the SYSTEM INetCache and its cmd.exe child wrote the marker.

registry.assessment: The strongest registry signal was JScriptSetScriptStateStarted beneath Windows Script telemetry for regsvr32.exe; generic Internet Settings and notification writes were not promoted alone.

process_identity.assessment: Sysmon captured regsvr32 identity, hashes, remote /i URL, scrobj.dll, SYSTEM user, and System integrity.

parent_child.assessment: PowerShell launched regsvr32 through the lab wrapper, and the scriptlet caused regsvr32 to launch cmd.exe directly.

evidence.description: Sanitized process, ancestry, endpoint network, file, and registry fields.
Sanitized full-packet capture metadata and Zeek/Suricata HTTP findings.
